key_insight: Some classically polynomial-time graph properties cannot be computed by polynomial-size symmetric quantum circuits whose entanglement width is o(n/log n), even with unrestricted depth.
engineering_relevance: For symmetry-preserving quantum circuit design, entanglement width is a provable resource bottleneck that additional depth alone cannot overcome.
method: Define entanglement width through the largest factor block needed after each layer on computational-basis inputs.
Introduce a partial-trace quantum pebble game to transfer classical indistinguishability lower bounds.
Construct symmetric circuits for BQP graph properties without entanglement restrictions and an efficient symmetric QAOA implementation for MAX 3XOR.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical proofs and circuit constructions, not experimental benchmarks; the lower bound covers arbitrary one- and two-qubit gates and even-permutation symmetry.
watch_item: The lower bound applies to symmetric circuit families, not unrestricted quantum circuits, and does not establish a practical QAOA advantage.
paper_title: Entanglement Lower Bounds for Symmetric Quantum Circuits
